reference.source: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology / Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics
clinicalPearls: The most severe form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia, most often caused by mutations in the StAR gene
Steroidogenesis is globally impaired, so all adrenal and gonadal steroid classes are markedly deficient
Classically presents in the newborn period with a life-threatening salt-wasting adrenal crisis
46,XY individuals are typically undervirilised with female-appearing external genitalia because testicular androgen synthesis fails
46,XX individuals have normal female external genitalia and may retain some ovarian function until puberty
Lipid accumulates in steroidogenic cells, producing the characteristic enlarged, lipid-laden adrenal glands that give the disorder its name
A non-classic milder variant can present later with more limited adrenal insufficiency
reference.pathophysiology: The steroidogenic acute regulatory protein (StAR) transports cholesterol into mitochondria, the essential first committed step for synthesising all steroid hormones. When StAR function is lost, cholesterol cannot be delivered for conversion, so production of glucocorticoids, mineralocorticoids and sex steroids fails across the adrenal cortex and gonads. Cholesterol and its esters accumulate within steroidogenic cells, causing the swollen lipid-laden glands and progressive cellular damage that further impairs any residual steroidogenesis. Because androgen synthesis fails, 46,XY fetuses do not virilise and are born with female-appearing genitalia.
additionalDifferentials: Other forms of congenital adrenal hyperplasia such as 21-hydroxylase deficiency
Adrenal insufficiency of other genetic causes
Disorders of cholesterol synthesis affecting steroidogenesis
additionalInvestigations: Serum electrolytes and glucose to detect salt wasting and hypoglycaemia
Paired cortisol and ACTH demonstrating adrenal insufficiency
Plasma renin and aldosterone to assess mineralocorticoid deficiency
Karyotype and pelvic imaging to define sex chromosomes and internal anatomy
Molecular genetic testing of StAR and related steroidogenic genes
redFlags: Neonatal salt-wasting adrenal crisis with hypotension, hyponatraemia and hyperkalaemia
Hypoglycaemia and collapse in a newborn from severe glucocorticoid deficiency
A 46,XY infant with female-appearing genitalia requiring urgent diagnostic evaluation
Any intercurrent illness precipitating acute adrenal decompensation
reference.prognosis: Survival depends on prompt recognition and lifelong glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement with stress dosing during illness; gonadal steroid replacement is needed at puberty, and fertility is generally severely impaired.
pitfalls: Failing to recognise a neonatal adrenal crisis quickly enough to prevent collapse
Assuming a phenotypically female newborn has a 46,XX karyotype without confirmation
Confusing lipoid CAH with milder forms of congenital adrenal hyperplasia
Neglecting stress-dose glucocorticoid cover during illness or surgery
management: Lifelong glucocorticoid replacement with hydrocortisone for cortisol deficiency
Mineralocorticoid replacement with fludrocortisone plus sodium chloride supplementation for salt wasting
Emergency stress dosing with parenteral hydrocortisone, fluids and glucose during illness, with family training and an injectable steroid emergency plan
Sex-steroid replacement with oestrogen or testosterone from the age of puberty
Multidisciplinary sex assignment and gonadal management for undervirilised 46,XY individuals, with surveillance for gonadal tumour risk
Regular monitoring of electrolytes, growth, blood pressure and pubertal development
Genetic counselling and family testing for autosomal recessive StAR inheritance
